scope: Henrietta missing-chicken poster, CS2 pet infrastructure, owner hypothesis, cultural antecedents

evidence_policy.confirmed: runtime observation, primary source, or directly inspectable public artifact
evidence_policy.hypothesis: search guidance only until an explicit bridge is found

henrietta_poster.name: Henrietta
text_semantics: reward for capture alive and unharmed
henrietta_poster.visual_detail: Henrietta is depicted wearing a collar
henrietta_poster.note: The collar is directly relevant to pet interpretation.

pet_infrastructure_context.m_iPetPopulation: map-level pet population field; server-side field predates Train release, client CMapInfo exposure was visible in the Train return build
pet_infrastructure_context.pet_hen_1: five Catalan adult hen econ render variants are packaged
pet_infrastructure_context.chick_branch: juvenile chick animations and Chicken.Chick.Interact audio exist
pet_infrastructure_context.nameable_path: popup_capability_nameable and pet-specific nameable handling exist
pet_infrastructure_context.placement: cs_pet_placement exists as a map placement marker class
pet_infrastructure_context.inventory: GetPetItemID / pet slot / petindex form a separate econ-pet architecture

user_hypothesis.statement: Henrietta must have an owner; candidate proposed by user: Gabe Newell
user_hypothesis.reason_to_keep: Valve frequently uses Gabe Newell as an in-universe/easter-egg figure, but no direct Henrietta-owner evidence has been found yet.

new_high_interest_cultural_bridge.author: Daniel Manus Pinkwater
confirmed_parallel_elements: The central chicken is named Henrietta.
Henrietta is treated as a pet/companion rather than an ordinary ambient chicken.
Henrietta is explicitly associated with a leash and collar in the book.
Henrietta escapes and becomes the subject of a town-wide search/capture effort.
The story is explicitly built around Thanksgiving and acquiring a bird for Thanksgiving dinner.
new_high_interest_cultural_bridge.temporal_resonance: CS2 Train with the missing Henrietta poster shipped in mid-November 2024, shortly before U.S. Thanksgiving.

gabe_name_coincidence.fact: The 1984 TV adaptation cast includes actor Gabe Kaplan.
gabe_name_coincidence.important_correction: Gabe Kaplan is not Gabe Newell and is not Henrietta's owner in the story.

new_high_interest_cultural_bridge.why_it_matters: The combined match is substantially stronger than the name alone: Henrietta + chicken + collar/leash + escape/search + November/Thanksgiving context.

current_model.ambient_chicken_system: separate and already sufficient for ordinary roaming chickens
current_model.pet_system: architecturally distinct; appears designed for owner/econ/name/placement/preview semantics
current_model.henrietta_interpretation: more likely a narrative breadcrumb for an owned/named chicken-pet concept than a simple hidden ambient NPC

priority_gates.pass: Any Valve/Train asset, metadata, texture, localization, source-control, or developer reference directly links the poster to The Hoboken Chicken Emergency.
A direct asset/code/lore bridge identifies Henrietta's owner.
Poster source metadata or artist commentary establishes intended reference.
A real callsite connects equipped pet inventory to map pet placement/chicken entity.

falsification.hoboken_bridge: Downgrade if poster image/text provenance is found and demonstrably unrelated, or if artist notes identify another source.
falsification.gaben_owner: Reject unless a direct Valve artifact or developer statement names Gabe Newell as owner; thematic association alone is insufficient.
